items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline gives the trade both ways: 30% cheaper, $7,560 a month, 6.1 points less in character, and nothing declared to weigh them. The flag gives the choice to the product owner. The decision slots give the price per point with its band ($1,239, $1,036 to $1,543) and which way each side goes. They add a labelled lean (keep Production until a re-run confirms f64's guardrails, at 8.9% and 9.7% wrong-side) and the main risks in Watch: specul cleared by 1.4 points, character loss unmeasured on listeners. c1 shows both axes.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 to c5 run in order: the trade, where the loss may sit (a lead), why f64 is the only option, how thin its clearance is, and minor gains. The headline is no longer contradicted. Two pieces still disagree. (a) next[0] says a declared price or margin 'turns the trade into a decision at once, with no further run'. where_it_flips and Explore row 1 leave the $1,036 to $1,543 band undecided, and our_lean keeps Production even below $1,036 until a re-run confirms the guardrails. (b) Method says a rate that clears its line while its interval crosses it 'goes in Watch'. f64's music-facts rate (92.1%, interval 89.0% to 95.2%, line 90%) is such a rate. Watch names only declining to speculate, as f64's 'nearest line'.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Both options' weak axes are visible: Production's $7,560 a month, and f64's 6.1-point loss and thin clearances of 2.1 and 1.4 points (c3, c4). The depth pattern is now a lead. One framing is stronger than the page supports. where_it_flips and both Explore rows rest on the paired interval -7.3 to -4.9, half-width 1.2. The report argues that per-reply intervals read too narrow because replies share conversations (c2 caption, Method 'Intervals'), yet it never says what unit this interval counts. The snapshot does not state it. Its own case-level spread (settle_cases: n = 300 cases per arm, about 8 replies each) gives roughly -11.2 to -1.0 unpaired. A clustered paired interval would fall between the two. The direction holds either way (settle wrong_side 0.9%), but the flip band could be several times wider than $1,036 to $1,543.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: I checked the omitted rows against the snapshot, and none changes the decision. The scenario strata hold no counts or shares (measure_breakdown returns none). The output-cap lever is -1.3 points (-7 to +4.4) between f64 and f16, not separated. No failure examples were kept (examples_list is empty). f16 and cor are out by the declared gates (options_dominance: f16 fails facts at -0.6, cor fails specul at -3). Production's own depth decline (93.5% to 87.5%) is descriptive. One small gap: omitted row 7 says the trial count behind each depth band is in Method, but Method gives only 300 cases and 2,400 replies per arm, not the band counts (912, 768, 480, 240).

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Each block fits its claim, and each counterfactual holds. c1: the cost bars and the persona forest would contradict the claim if f64 were dearer or its interval crossed zero. c3: the guardrail dot-intervals against their floors would contradict it if f64's dots fell under 90% or 95%. c4: the settle bars carry exactly the 8.9% and 9.7% the claim cites. c5: the latency range bars. One defect remains, listed in findings. c2's caption says no intervals are drawn because per-reply intervals overstate how settled each band is. Its rendered note still says 'Bold rows are separated at 95% before any correction', which marks rows as separated using exactly those intervals.

findings.finding: The flip band rests on an interval whose unit the page never states. where_it_flips ($1,036 to $1,543) and Explore rows 1 and 2 (4.9 to 7.3 points) both come from the paired contrast -7.3 to -4.9. The report itself argues that per-reply intervals read too narrow because about 8 replies share each of 300 conversations, but it applies that argument only to the depth bands. The snapshot does not say whether this contrast counts conversations or replies. Read on cases, the unpaired spread is about -11.2 to -1.0. The direction holds either way (wrong_side 0.9%), but the band could be several times wider. Say in Method and where_it_flips that the band is the pipeline's paired interval with its unit unstated, and that it would widen if it counts replies.

next[0]'s settles clause, 'Turns the trade into a decision at once, with no further run', contradicts the page. Between $1,036 and $1,543 a point (or a 4.9 to 7.3 point margin), where_it_flips and Explore say this run can't tell. Below $1,036, our_lean still keeps Production until a re-run confirms the guardrails. Say that a declaration settles the call outright only above the high end. Elsewhere it settles the call once next[1]'s re-run confirms f64, or it narrows the call to the middle band.

Method says a rate that clears its line while its interval crosses it 'goes in Watch'. f64's music-facts rate (92.1%, 89.0% to 95.2%, line 90%) is borderline by that rule, but Watch names only declining to speculate, as the 'nearest line'. Add music facts, cleared by {criteria.facts.f64.gap|abs|pts}, to Watch, or soften Method's rule.

The caption says no intervals are drawn because per-reply intervals overstate how settled each band is. The block's own note says 'Bold rows are separated at 95% before any correction', and those bold marks come from the same per-reply intervals. A reader sees the page disown intervals and then use them. Drop the separation marking for this block, or say in the caption that the bold marks rest on per-reply intervals and are as unsettled as the bands.

Omitted row 7 says the trial count behind each depth band is in Method, but it is not there. Method gives 300 cases and 2,400 replies per arm, not the band counts (912, 768, 480, 240 replies, or 38%, 32%, 20% and 10%). Those shares also matter to next[2]'s mix: the 6–10 and 11+ bands hold 30% of replies but about two thirds of f64's 6.1-point loss.
